newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain small business group welcomes corp tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Spain small business group welcomes corp tax cut.

text.p: The Spanish Association of small- and medium-sized business CEPYME said on Tuesday it welcomed news the ruling Popular Party planned cuts in corporate tax rates for smaller business.

"This step is, without a doubt, a key step in improving the taxation of companies that, for CEPYME, create incentives for individuals and businesses which are the major pillar of employment in the country," CEPYME said in a statement.

The government said it would present an amendment to the budget that would cut the tax rate on businesses that invoice less than 250 million pesetas a year to 30 percent from 35 percent on their initial 15 million pesetas in profit.
"For CEPYME, the step is favourable for business activity and resolves a comparable disadvantage that had been produced with Basque legislation in this area," the association said in a statement.
The Basque country, which enjoys broader historic taxation rights than its fellow regions, set corporate tax rates that other regions and companies based elsewhere found disadvantageous.
"CEPYME thinks that substantial improvement has been made this year in taxation of small- and medium-sized companies," the statement said.
